title: Virtual FOG conjecture
exact_target: Do finite-order inert automorphisms generate a subgroup of finite index in the inert automorphism group of every mixing SFT?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $A$ be a primitive nonnegative integral matrix and $(X_A,\sigma)$
its mixing edge shift. Write $\operatorname{Aut}(X_A,\sigma)$ for the
group of homeomorphisms commuting with $\sigma$. The ordered dimension
group is $G_A=\varinjlim(\mathbb Z^N,v\mapsto vA)$, with its cone
represented by nonnegative vectors and its automorphism
$\delta_A[v,j]=[vA,j]$.

Each shift automorphism $\phi$ acts on this group, giving the dimension
representation $\rho_A$. Concretely, an elementary strong shift
equivalence $A=UV$, $B=VU$ induces $[v,j]\mapsto[vU,j]$; decomposing
a conjugacy into these steps and a shift power defines its induced map,
independently of the decomposition. Define the inert subgroup
\[
 \operatorname{Aut}_0(X_A)=\ker\rho_A,
 \qquad
 F_0(X_A)=\langle\phi\in\operatorname{Aut}_0(X_A):
                      \phi^r=\operatorname{id}\text{ for some }r\ge1\rangle.
\]
The subgroup $F_0$ is normal, since conjugation preserves finite order
and preserves the inert subgroup.

The virtual finite-order-generation conjecture asks whether
\[
 |\operatorname{Aut}_0(X_A)/F_0(X_A)|<\infty
\]
for every mixing SFT. The finite quotient may depend on $A$; there is
no proposed uniform bound. Generation allows arbitrary finite products
of finite-order inert automorphisms, without a common order bound.
The stronger assertion $F_0=\operatorname{Aut}_0$ is not requested:
the source records counterexamples to that earlier conjecture. Nor
does the statement claim that every element of $F_0$ itself has finite
order. It asks only for finite index of the subgroup generated by
all such elements.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Do finite-order inert automorphisms generate a subgroup of finite index in the inert automorphism group of every mixing SFT?
